[Kevin Trinh] 11:16:04 Sure. So, uh, outgoing subawards. So this is when we have a prime award, so we're the prime recipient, and part of the scope of work is going to be performed by another institution. So we issue a subaward to them.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:16:22 And I want to be clear up front that there's a proposal-stage version of this and an award-stage version of this, and they're different, and people conflate them constantly. Um, I'll do the award stage, because that's the one that's, that's where the pain is.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:16:39 So.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:16:41 Uh, it starts with a request. And the request should come from the department, from the fund manager, uh, on behalf of the PI.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:16:51 And I say should, because sometimes it comes from the PI directly, sometimes it comes as a reply to an unrelated email thread from four months ago, and, uh, and once in a while the first we hear about it is when somebody asks why the sub hasn't been paid.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:17:08 Um.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:17:10 So the intake, the formal intake, is a form in, uh, in our research administration system. We're on Kuali Research, uh, K-U-A-L-I. Uh, though a lot of people still call the module by the old name.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:17:26 And what we need on that form is the statement of work for the sub, the budget and budget justification, the period of performance, the PI at the subrecipient institution, and the, um, and the F&A rate agreement.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:17:42 And I would estimate that maybe thirty percent of requests come in complete.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:17:48 So the rest, we go back. And that back and forth is, um, that's usually one to three rounds of email. Because you ask for the statement of work, and they send you the proposal narrative, and the proposal narrative is not a statement of work.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:18:05 Um, once we have a complete package.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:18:09 The next piece is the risk assessment. So under Uniform Guidance we're required to evaluate the subrecipient's risk of noncompliance. And how we do that is, uh, we use the FDP clearinghouse entity profile if the institution is in there.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:18:26 If they're in the clearinghouse, that's, that's easy, it's maybe twenty minutes. That covers most domestic universities.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:18:34 If they're not in the clearinghouse, and this is small nonprofits, foreign institutions, some companies, then we send them our own questionnaire.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:18:44 And then we're waiting on them. And, um, and the waiting is not bounded by anything. I have one right now that's been out for, uh, I want to say five weeks.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:18:56 So then based on the risk assessment we decide whether they need any special terms. Uh, more frequent reporting, invoice detail requirements, sometimes we'll withhold a percentage until the final report.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:19:11 Um, and separately, in parallel, uh, they have to exist as a payee in the financial system. So if it's a first-time subrecipient, there's a supplier onboarding process, and that's, that's a different office. That's not us.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:19:28 And that one is, um, that's a place where things stall out and we don't have visibility into it. I can see that the request is in, I can't see where in the queue it is.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:19:40 Uh, so then we draft the agreement.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:19:44 We use the FDP subaward template for federal flow-down, that's the standard, and that's, that's the good case, because the terms are pre-negotiated across the membership. Most institutions will sign it without changes.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:19:59 For nonfederal primes, foundations and industry, uh, we're building the terms from the prime agreement, and every prime is different. So we're reading the prime award, pulling the flow-down obligations, publication rights, IP, data, audit, and drafting those into the sub.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:20:19 That's a couple of hours of actual drafting for a straightforward one and, um, and considerably more if there's IP complexity.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:20:29 Then it goes out for their review. And they redline. Um, common redlines are indemnification, governing law, publication delay periods.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:20:41 Uh, foreign subrecipients add export control, and if there's any human subjects or animal work, there's an IRB or IACUC reliance question that has to be resolved before we can fully execute, and that's its own process with its own timeline that I don't control.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:20:59 So negotiation is, uh, honestly it's anywhere from zero rounds to, I've had eight.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:21:07 Uh, once we're agreed on language, it goes for signature. We use DocuSign. Uh, our authorized official signs, theirs signs, and, um, and getting a signature at some institutions is quick and at others it's two weeks.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:21:24 Once it's fully executed, then two things happen. We file the executed agreement, uh, and we notify the department so they can request the purchase order. Because the sub can't be paid without a PO encumbering the funds.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:21:39 And that PO request is on the department, not on us, and, um, and sometimes they don't do it. And then we get the call about why the sub hasn't been paid.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:21:51 So that's setup. There's also the ongoing part, which is invoices.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:21:57 So the sub invoices us, uh, typically monthly or quarterly. And the PI has to approve the invoice, which is a technical judgment, is the work being performed, are the costs reasonable for the progress.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:22:12 And the fund manager reviews it against the budget and the period of performance.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:22:17 Um, the pain point here is invoice format. There is no standard. Some come in as PDFs on letterhead with a cost breakdown, some come in as a one-line email that says "please remit $47,000."
[Kevin Trinh] 11:22:33 And we have to send those back, because we need cumulative to date, current period, and a certification. Uh, and that back and forth delays payment, and then the sub PI calls our PI, and our PI calls me.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:22:48 Uh, and then closeout. Final invoice, final technical report, uh, any property or invention reporting, and we have to close the sub before we can close the prime. And subs closing late is one of the main reasons primes close late.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:23:06 Um, and I'll say the thing that's missing across all of it is a single view of status. I have a spreadsheet. It has about, uh, ninety active subawards on it, and I update it by hand.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:23:20 And if a chair asks me where their department's five subs are, I'm reading email to answer that.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:23:27 So, recapping. Request comes in from the department, usually incomplete, we chase the missing pieces. Risk assessment, clearinghouse if we're lucky, questionnaire if we're not. Supplier onboarding in parallel if they're new.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:23:43 Draft the agreement, FDP template for federal, custom for everything else. Send for their review, negotiate redlines. Signature through DocuSign both sides. Notify the department to request the PO.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:23:58 Then ongoing invoice review, PI approval, fund manager check. Then closeout.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:05 Times. Um.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:08 Intake and completeness chasing, thirty minutes if it's clean, two to three hours spread across a week or two if it's not.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:17 Risk assessment, twenty minutes clearinghouse, uh, and then one to six weeks of calendar time if we're waiting on a questionnaire, though the hands-on work is maybe an hour.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:29 Drafting, one hour for a standard FDP federal sub, three to eight hours for a nonfederal or complex one.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:38 Negotiation, that's the wide one. Zero to twenty hours of my time, and two weeks to four months of calendar.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:47 Signature routing, an hour of work, one to three weeks of waiting.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:24:52 Invoice review is maybe twenty minutes each when they're formatted right and an hour when they're not, times ninety active subs, times however many invoices a year each.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:25:05 Closeout is two to four hours.
[Kevin Trinh] 11:25:09 Um, and end to end, from request to executed agreement, our median is somewhere around forty five days. And the target people expect is thirty. So we're, we're behind expectation on the median and the tail is much worse than the median.
